data-contracts.brief: The batch-request changeset has an internal count limit of 4 in Limits.max/0; Batch.submit/1 uses this module and returns :accepted or {:error, :too_many}. A view currently repeats the number in wording; views may depend on Batch only. Deliver all three small modules Limits, Batch and View. The public view function View.hint/0 returns "Up to 4 entries" today. The product still promises four, but maintaining the number in two places caused a regression. Accept any list of entries, including an empty list.
data-contracts.oracle: Unique numeric owner; facade accessor consumed by the hint; actual boundary +/-1 plus changing owner must move both consumers.
data-contracts.checks:
assert Batch.submit([]) == :accepted
assert Batch.submit([1,2,3,4]) == :accepted
assert Batch.submit([1,2,3,4,5]) == {:error,:too_many}
assert View.hint() == "Up to 4 entries"

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Limits do
  def max, do: 4
end

defmodule Batch do
  def max_entries, do: Limits.max()

  def submit(entries) when is_list(entries) do
    if length(entries) <= max_entries() do
      :accepted
    else
      {:error, :too_many}
    end
  end
end

defmodule View do
  def hint, do: "Up to #{Batch.max_entries()} entries"
end

migration-compatibility.brief: We are midway through introducing a stable reference into a snapshot. Old readers require the :label field. New readers use :ref when available, otherwise can obtain an optional reference from the linked source. Some old rows have lost their source; some are supported platform records for which a ref does not exist by design. A runner must survive mixed data and restarts, and cannot discard snapshot fields from the previous version. Implement Upgrade.row(snapshot, linked_ref, kind) -> {outcome, snapshot} for :ordinary or :platform records; outcomes are :updated, :unchanged or :unresolved. Write a brief deployment/rollback decision for whether the dual reader can be retired today. No production inventory or rollout evidence is supplied.
migration-compatibility.oracle: Preserve unknown/legacy fields; idempotent no overwrite; unresolved orphan not fabricated, platform exempt; require writer rollout/backfill reconciliation with unresolved handled before destructive cutoff.

provider-calls.brief: A mail relay sometimes rejects the connection for hours. Three tries within one minute lose messages. Status calls can establish a pre-delivery failure, a permanent refusal, confirmed delivery, or an ambiguous result after submission. This provider has no deduplication API. Re-granting a resource to the same person later is a legitimate new event, even when the audit key (recipient plus resource) repeats. The approved outage budget is five total attempts; delay after each of the first four attempts is 1, 10, 60 or 360 minutes. Deliver Relay.next(status, attempt, seen_audit_key?) as a policy for an existing job, returning {:retry_in, seconds}, :complete, :failed or :reconcile. Status is :temporary_before_send, :permanent, :delivered, or :unknown_after_send. Indicate what the worker must store or do with ambiguous results.
provider-calls.oracle: Transient schedule seconds and finite stop; no uncertain resend; repeats of audit keys cannot blanket suppress a new event; permanent/confirmed are terminal.
provider-calls.checks:
for seen <- [true,false] do
 assert Enum.map(1..4, &Relay.next(:temporary_before_send,&1,seen)) == [{:retry_in,60},{:retry_in,600},{:retry_in,3600},{:retry_in,21600}]
 assert Relay.next(:temporary_before_send,5,seen) == :failed
 assert Relay.next(:permanent,1,seen) == :failed
 assert Relay.next(:delivered,1,seen) == :complete
 assert Relay.next(:unknown_after_send,2,seen) == :reconcile
end

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Relay do
  @retry_delays {60, 600, 3_600, 21_600}

  @type status ::
          :temporary_before_send
          | :permanent
          | :delivered
          | :unknown_after_send

  @spec next(status(), 1..5, boolean()) ::
          {:retry_in, pos_integer()} | :complete | :failed | :reconcile
  def next(status, attempt, _seen_audit_key?)
      when is_integer(attempt) and attempt >= 1 and attempt <= 5 do
    case status do
      :temporary_before_send when attempt < 5 ->
        {:retry_in, elem(@retry_delays, attempt - 1)}

      :temporary_before_send ->
        :failed

      :permanent ->
        :failed

      :delivered ->
        :complete

      :unknown_after_send ->
        :reconcile
    end
  end
end
returned_modules.b:
defmodule Relay do
  @type status ::
          :temporary_before_send | :permanent | :delivered | :unknown_after_send

  @type decision :: {:retry_in, pos_integer()} | :complete | :failed | :reconcile

  @retry_delays_seconds {60, 600, 3_600, 21_600}

  @spec next(status(), 1..5, boolean()) :: decision()
  def next(status, attempt, seen_audit_key?)
      when status in [
             :temporary_before_send,
             :permanent,
             :delivered,
             :unknown_after_send
           ] and
             is_integer(attempt) and attempt >= 1 and attempt <= 5 and
             is_boolean(seen_audit_key?) do
    case status do
      :delivered ->
        :complete

      :permanent ->
        :failed

      :unknown_after_send ->
        :reconcile

      :temporary_before_send when attempt < 5 ->
        {:retry_in, elem(@retry_delays_seconds, attempt - 1)}

      :temporary_before_send ->
        :failed
    end
  end
end

data-pipelines.brief: An old batch conversion walks records sorted by strictly increasing integer id. Convert a manually marked :settled item into :waived only when the ledger has no recorded transfer, even a refunded one. Bank-marked items must stay settled even if the charge link vanished. A retained item still matches the current read predicate, so a worker asking only for the first N qualifying records can loop. Implement Walk.page(rows, after_id, limit) yielding {ids_to_convert, next_cursor}; rows are {id, status, manual?, evidence}, evidence one of :none, :settled, :refunded, :legacy. Fetch the next limit manually marked settled candidates by id (the query applies both predicates); on a nonempty page return the highest examined candidate ID even if no IDs may be converted, else :done. State the update condition that avoids overwriting another actor after paging and how a restarting worker makes progress.
data-pipelines.oracle: Page includes retained rows; monotonic progression on all-retained page, bounded sorted window, protects bank/ledger provenance; apply guarded updates and advance checkpoint only after durable success.

abstraction-layers.brief: Simplify a single toggle operation that mixes a decision about an existing connection, saving it, and post-success effects. A minimal harness injects callbacks through a map. Preserve Link.toggle(a,b,ops): ops.lookup.(a,b) yields nil or a record. If nil, ops.insert.(a,b) returns {:ok,row} or {:error,reason}; only on success call ops.notice.(a,b) then ops.broadcast.(a,b), and return {:ok,:on}. Otherwise call ops.delete.(record) once and return {:ok,:off}; the existing delete path ignores its return value, and performs no notifications. Keep this to one module; make the top-level operation easier to read without changing its contract.
abstraction-layers.oracle: Separate decision from lower-level persistence/announcement; unchanged result and ordered effects on successful create, error create and failed delete.
abstraction-layers.checks:
for {record,insert,answer,trace} <- [{nil,{:ok,:new},{:ok,:on},[:lookup,:insert,:notice,:broadcast]},{nil,{:error,:collision},{:error,:collision},[:lookup,:insert]},{:old,:unused,{:ok,:off},[:lookup,:delete]}] do
 Process.put(:events,[])
 f=fn k -> Process.put(:events,Process.get(:events)++[k]) end
 ops=%{lookup: fn :a,:b -> f.(:lookup); record end,insert: fn :a,:b -> f.(:insert); insert end,notice: fn :a,:b -> f.(:notice) end,broadcast: fn :a,:b -> f.(:broadcast) end,delete: fn :old -> f.(:delete); {:error,:stale} end}
 assert Link.toggle(:a,:b,ops) == answer
 assert Process.get(:events) == trace
end

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Link do
  def toggle(a, b, ops) do
    case ops.lookup.(a, b) do
      nil ->
        turn_on(a, b, ops)

      record ->
        ops.delete.(record)
        {:ok, :off}
    end
  end

  defp turn_on(a, b, ops) do
    case ops.insert.(a, b) do
      {:ok, _row} ->
        ops.notice.(a, b)
        ops.broadcast.(a, b)
        {:ok, :on}

      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end
end
returned_modules.b:
defmodule Link do
  def toggle(a, b, ops) do
    case ops.lookup.(a, b) do
      nil -> turn_on(a, b, ops)
      record -> turn_off(record, ops)
    end
  end

  defp turn_on(a, b, ops) do
    case ops.insert.(a, b) do
      {:ok, _row} ->
        ops.notice.(a, b)
        ops.broadcast.(a, b)
        {:ok, :on}

      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp turn_off(record, ops) do
    ops.delete.(record)
    {:ok, :off}
  end
end

module-design.brief: A storage adapter imports CatalogTile just to build the existing disk key, yet the catalogue already needs the adapter for public URLs. The codebase has a downward dependency rule: Storage must not depend on CatalogTile. There are no external callers of the historical key/subdirectory helpers. Deliver minimal replacements for both modules. The facade contracts that must survive are CatalogTile.url(%{slug: "a"}) -> "/assets/tiles/a.svg", and Storage.upload("a", writer) -> whatever writer.("tiles/a.svg") returns. Existence checks and seed jobs need one canonical key derived from a plain slug at Storage.key/1. The adapter's public_url/1 simply prefixes "/assets/".
module-design.oracle: Storage owns key; catalog reads simple key without reverse dependency or duplicate builder; existing read and write paths use identical stored key and pass through writer result.

code-consolidation.brief: Three entry points have local copies of the normalization of a person's display name. Registration.clean/1 and Profile.clean/1 return a value; Account.change/1 accepts a map of changes and must touch :name only if present; account changes also include unrelated :title which explicitly retains surrounding blanks. PersonLabel already owns the validation of display names. Deliver the four small modules (include only relevant functions). Consolidate normalization there, preserving nil, all internal spacing and the spelling of a name. Leading/trailing whitespace is not intentional.
code-consolidation.oracle: One named domain owner, all three callers, nil, original internal spaces, no insertion of missing change and no alteration of unrelated fields.

house-patterns.brief: A narrow style guard rejected Panel.refresh/4. The written local rule is one pipeline stage per line and a raw value at the start; a pipeline may be kept across multiple dependent transformations. Existing modules follow this. Current intended behavior: if requested == state.current, return state; otherwise start with state, then call put_current(requested), then invoke load.(updated_state). The injected put_current/2 helper sets :current using Map.put/3; it is passed as the third argument, and load as the fourth. Write the corrected Panel.refresh(state, requested, put_current, load) and keep the guard's pattern visible. No other style changes are necessary.
house-patterns.oracle: One pipe per physical line, raw start, unchanged no-op, assign before one reload, no architecture detour.

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Panel do
  def refresh(state, requested, put_current, load) do
    if requested == state.current do
      state
    else
      state
      |> put_current.(requested)
      |> load.()
    end
  end
end

functional-refactoring.brief: Public CalendarFacade.over?(month, local_today) takes a Date plus a zero-arity function reading today's local date; Withdraw.deadline/1 should return a UTC DateTime exactly three hours before the supplied one or nil. In the real module other operations read records; the calendar-only rules need isolated tests and currently share the effects module. Preserve these public signatures, keep the local clock read at its edge once, and move date calculations into a pure Period module. For a monthly record the entire final local calendar day is still active. Include additional pure helper Period.month_of(local_date) returning the first day of its month. Only submit these three small modules.
functional-refactoring.oracle: Current month still active on final day; previous month over on first local day; edge clock read once; pure helper and nil, UTC deadline, no DB/clock in calculations.
functional-refactoring.checks:
assert Period.month_of(~D[2024-02-29])==~D[2024-02-01]
for {today,expected} <- [{~D[2024-02-29],false},{~D[2024-03-01],true}] do
 assert CalendarFacade.over?(~D[2024-02-07],fn -> send(self(),:clock); today end)==expected
 assert_receive :clock
 refute_receive :clock,0
end
assert Withdraw.deadline(nil)==nil
assert DateTime.compare(Withdraw.deadline(~U[2024-03-01 01:00:00Z]),~U[2024-02-29 22:00:00Z])==:eq

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Period do
  @spec month_of(Date.t()) :: Date.t()
  def month_of(%Date{} = local_date) do
    Date.beginning_of_month(local_date)
  end

  @spec over?(Date.t(), Date.t()) :: boolean()
  def over?(%Date{} = month, %Date{} = local_today) do
    Date.compare(local_today, Date.end_of_month(month)) == :gt
  end
end

defmodule CalendarFacade do
  @spec over?(Date.t(), (() -> Date.t())) :: boolean()
  def over?(%Date{} = month, local_today) when is_function(local_today, 0) do
    today = local_today.()
    Period.over?(month, today)
  end
end

defmodule Withdraw do
  @spec deadline(DateTime.t() | nil) :: DateTime.t() | nil
  def deadline(nil), do: nil

  def deadline(%DateTime{} = supplied) do
    supplied
    |> DateTime.shift_zone!("Etc/UTC")
    |> DateTime.add(-10_800, :second)
  end
end

  def over?(%Date{} = month, %Date{} = local_today) do

  end

  @spec month_of(Date.t()) :: Date.t()
  def month_of(%Date{} = local_date), do: %{local_date | day: 1}

  @spec deadline(DateTime.t() | nil) :: DateTime.t() | nil

  def deadline(%DateTime{} = datetime) do

    |> DateTime.add(-10_800, :second)

    Period.over?(month, today)
  end
end

defmodule Withdraw do
  @spec deadline(DateTime.t() | nil) :: DateTime.t() | nil
  def deadline(datetime), do: Period.deadline(datetime)
end

readable-code.brief: A nested lookup followed by integer parsing makes a public metadata counter hard to read. Keep Meta.count(key, lookup) where lookup is a single-argument function returning nil or a binary; absence or nonnumeric content maps to zero. Existing persisted text may start with a signed integer followed by a suffix, and that numeric prefix counts as the value. Simplify without changing public results, number of lookups or the lookup exception contract. Submit only the module and explain how the reading obstacle was removed.
readable-code.oracle: Extract private meaning or equivalent flat flow; preserves nil/unparsable/prefix/signed/leading space behavior and exceptions; exactly one lookup.
readable-code.checks:
for {s,n} <- [{nil,0},{"bad",0},{"-2x",-2},{"+17z",17},{" 7",0},{"",0},{"9",9}] do
 assert Meta.count(:key,fn :key -> send(self(),:lookup); s end)==n
 assert_receive :lookup
 refute_receive :lookup,0
end
assert_raise RuntimeError,fn -> Meta.count(:key,fn _ -> raise "down" end) end

returned_modules.a:
defmodule Meta do
  def count(key, lookup) do
    key
    |> lookup.()
    |> parse_count()
  end

  defp parse_count(nil), do: 0

  defp parse_count(text) when is_binary(text) do
    case Integer.parse(text) do
      {value, _suffix} -> value
      :error -> 0
    end
  end
end
